verdict.rationale: Three.js has abundant public examples, extensive docs, and even a dedicated llms.txt for AI consumption (threejs-probe-1, threejs-docs-9, threejs-docs-16), which should help LLMs generate working code for common tasks like scenes/renderers (threejs-gh-4). However, evidence also shows frequent breaking changes requiring migration guides across versions (threejs-docs-10, threejs-docs-17, threejs-gh-6) and community reports of real friction with seemingly simple tasks (obj loading took a week despite prior OpenGL experience: threejs-comm-3, threejs-comm-4) and TypeScript type mismatches (threejs-comm-6), which undercut 'mostly works on first try' claims for models trained on possibly-outdated API versions. Missing for 10: independent benchmark data on LLM code-gen success rate, evidence that frequent API changes don't stale out training-data examples, and resolution of the documented loader/type friction reports.
